question: Under two rules added by hand to the cheapest growth (at most three fresh distinctions; a knot that cannot pay waits) does a ring of an odd number of knots return to its start every two rounds while the same finite parts come apart from it, on real knots and by independent code; does every knot pass the canonical knot test in the whole structure under parity and not-all-equal; and what happens when each of the three added rules is swapped?
inputs: The registered rings; the shared definitions; the record's published counts for the gate.
forbidden_inputs: Any definition changed after a value is seen; any outcome of this study before the freeze; for the engine's author, the pilot's programs.
primary_observable: The live roster after every round: members, loose counts, witnessed sets, parts, lineage; the verdict of the knot test for every knot.
comparators_or_controls: Ordinary growth on the same rings; CAP-4 in place of CAP-3; a planted failing knot; the pilot's two programs.
resource_budget: Each run under ten minutes and 4 GB on one process; anything longer through the shared runner.
first_executable_signal: Row G of the predictions table.
decision_rule: Each prediction is judged by its 'Fails when' column.
stop_rule: The study stops when its registered runs are done and each prediction has a verdict.
nonclaims: An exploratory study of laws changed by hand (assumption A224) and of starts built by hand; every census and sample is finite and proves no all-size statement; no claim about ordinary growth beyond the cited records, and none about time, minds or living things.
